articles.title: Trails In The Sky 2nd Chapter Review
articles.summary: An impressive remake which captures everything that made the original so endearing.
body: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter picks up right where its predecessor ends with our bubbly and confident heroine, Estelle Bright. Now that her adoptive brother and best friend Joshua Bright suddenly recalled his true origins and has disappeared, Estelle is dead set on finding him and bringing him home. It also digs deeper and fleshes out the cultish revelations that were unearthed towards the end of 1st Chapter. As a result, it gives 2nd Chapter heavier stakes from onset, but also with the emotionally resonant edge that keeps you invested.

2nd Chapter is virtually a faithful 1:1 recreation of the original in terms of story structure and side quests, so you’ll be running around Liberl Kingdom going through the same cities and locations as you did in 1st Chapter. While that might seem like a rehash, the order in which you visit them in this sequel is rearranged. Along with a completely different slate of side quests to tackle from the previous adventure, it makes this journey feel much less like a retread and more like revisiting an old home.
points: An impressive remake which captures everything that made the original so endearing.

articles.title: Login errors delay Diablo 4's big new Season of Hell's Legacy anniversary update
articles.summary: The launch of Diablo 4 's Season of Hell's Legacy got off to a rough start. The anticipated season was announced at BlizzCon over the weekend to arrive alongside a 30th anniversary celebration of the Diablo franchise.
body: Players reported running into a number of login issues, with error codes 300006 and 300008 the most commonly reported. "We're aware of an issue preventing some players from accessing Diablo 4. The team is actively investigating and working to resolve the issue as quickly as possible," was the Diablo account's immediate response on X.

Two hours later, the Diablo account posted another update announcing the season launch delay, and Diablo 4 was entirely inaccessible throughout that period and for hours later. "We're continuing to address issues affecting today's launch of Season of Hell's Legacy. As a result, Season 15 is currently delayed. We appreciate your patience while we work to resolve the issues and we'll share updates as we have them."

It took another two hours for things to approve, with Blizzard confirming log in issues had been resolved, but some game features had to be temporarily disabled. The season ended up going live over six hours later.
points: The launch of Diablo 4 's Season of Hell's Legacy got off to a rough start.
The anticipated season was announced at BlizzCon over the weekend to arrive alongside a 30th anniversary celebration of the Diablo franchise.

articles.title: 10 BG3 Characters Fans Still Want as Companions
articles.summary: Baldur’s Gate 3 is full of moments like this: A great character, an intriguing story, and then no reliable way to learn what happens next. For Mizora — Wyll's patron devil, the one who granted him his warlock powers — a new mod has delivered a way around that issue.
body: A frustrating scene for your consideration: A paladin leads his people out of a burning camp, holds together the survivors of a massacre, and fights off Absolute cultists not once but twice…and then you just say goodbye? Here’s another: A druid nearly gets an entire grove slaughtered, spends the rest of the story trying to live with the consequences, and the game decides that's not compelling enough to keep them around. Excuse me?!
Why we’re inviting Alfira to camp: One song from her was simply never going to be enough.
Why we’re inviting Barcus to camp: He survived three acts of hell and still doesn't get a spot at the campfire?

Barcus is a gnome you rescue from a burning windmill early in Act 1, if you’re so inclined. After that, his life doesn’t exactly get easier. He’s captured (again), he’s tortured for information about his former friend Wulbren's whereabouts, dragged to Moonrise Towers, and finally handed leadership of the Ironhand clan in Act 3 after everyone else in charge lets him down. His arc gives him as much story as a companion — he just needs a class to build skills around. After everything he’s been through, he’s earned at least that much.

articles.title: Every Fourth Wing Board Game Adaption You Can Buy Right Now
articles.summary: Rebecca Yarros' Empyrean series has taken the romantasy genre by storm over the past few years. With three books so far, an upcoming graphic novel, and a TV show in the works, there's never been a better time to be a fan of Fourth Wing.
body: And while the TV series is likely the most exciting adaptation the books will ever see, Fourth Wing has already quietly been making its way into the tabletop space over the last couple of years. There are now four Fourth Wing board games you can buy, and probably more on their way.

The rise of romantasy tabletop games is a fairly recent thing. For the Empyrean series it all began with the release of Priorities Fourth Wing Edition last year. Since then we've gotten an original strategy game and two branded Monopoly games out of the franchise. This same tabletop arc also seems to be happening for Sarah J. Maas' ACOTAR series simultaneously.

Fourth Wing: Rise of the Wingleader is the only original board game for the series so far. Created by Goliath Games, Rise of the Wingleader is a strategy board game that incorporates cards with custom artwork, dragon pieces, and a round game board. You also get a nice metal bookmark alongside the board game itself.

articles.title: 'This Is a Place You Come to Work Hard' — Wardogs CEO Justifies Crunch as a Balancing Act
articles.summary: Joe Brammer, the CEO of Wardogs developer Bulkhead, has stated that the studio avoids hiring people who aren't willing to crunch. In an interview with The Game Business, Brammer was asked about the studio's approach to crunch. He noted that he values balance, but not in the way people may think.
body: "For the last three months, Wardogs has been a lot more important than a lot of their family lives," said Brammer. "It has been, because that's what pays the money for them. But now Bulkhead has to acknowledge that it needs to go the other way. For example, everyone is pushing us to get console out earlier.

"We've just said, 'No, you don't understand, that's not how it's going to work. We can't push them more. We're not doing that. It's going to release in 2028 when we say it's going to release.' So, for me it's about balance and helping people and making sure they have a company where they can say, 'I'm tapping out,' and not feel like they're going to get fired for tapping out."

Brammer went on to note that it has become harder to crunch due to the team getting older and trying to start families. He stated that they initially offered 10-week paternity leave, but eventually had to ditch it because the employees' partners were struggling to handle them going back to work. Instead, Bulkhead now offers 2-weeks of paternity leave and gives half-days to employees as a way of making the transition easier for the families.

articles.title: 10 Darkest 'Calvin and Hobbes' Snowman Jokes That Reveal Bill Watterson's Twisted Genius
articles.summary: Generally, when people think of Bill Watterson’s comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, they think of fun, innocent adventures with a little boy and his plush tiger, oftentimes exploring the woods or riding on a sled in the snow.
body: Calvin and Hobbes began on Nov. 18, 1985. While Watterson drew comic strips featuring snowmen in the first few years, on Feb. 28, 1988, he took a noticeably darker turn when he depicted a crowd of snowmen around the family car, as though there’d been a car accident. The beauty of the comic is the slow-burn, with Calvin seemingly-innocently making snowmen. Finally, in the last panel, the gruesome scene is revealed with his parents observing the scene, with Calvin’s dad saying, “I think we’d better get that kid to a psychologist.”

It would be almost a year before Watterson would go similarly dark with Calvin’s snowman sculptures, which is when it became a regular recurring series until the comic strip ended in 1995. Many of the strips featured death and destruction, even disturbing jokes about suicide that make you wonder how Calvin knew about this stuff. Some of the images were likely shocking, especially when juxtaposed against lighter comics like Peanuts or The Family Circus, but thanks to the multi-faceted personality Watterson crafted for Calvin, the dark jokes suited the character perfectly.
Here are the 10 darkest snowman gags that ever appeared in Calvin and Hobbes.

articles.title: I've been waiting all year for the 2nd Chapter to last year's best JRPG remake—it did not disappoint
articles.summary: I had an extremely good time with the Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter last year. As a big fan of the Trails of Cold Steel PC ports, finally getting the opportunity to try the first installment in the beloved JRPG series, with all the modern accoutrements of a full 3D remake, was truly a pleasure.
body: Falcom really didn't skimp when it came to upgrading the experience to the standard of its newer Trails games. There's only one problem: I wanted more.

Despite 1st Chapter being a pretty well-rounded story—clocking in at a perfectly reasonable 40 hours for me—it ends on a criminal cliffhanger. It's easy to see why so many say that 2nd Chapter is really just the second part of the first game, something I probably should've clocked considering the naming convention.

But having played Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter Remake this last week or so, I can say it feels more like a victory lap, building on the setting, characters, and quests you completed in the first. It's very much what you'd expect from the middle child of a JRPG trilogy—the cogs are turning, the characters moving, we're going somewhere.

While I won't spoil too much, 2nd Chapter feels like a bit more of a coming of age story for Estelle, as she finds herself adrift as a newly-made Senior Bracer. With the help of familiar faces, you'll travel around Liberl investigating the activities of Ouroborous, the secret society who reared their head in the previous game.
points: I had an extremely good time with the Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter last year.

articles.title: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter has one of the creepiest JRPG monsters I've encountered
articles.summary: Let's face it: JRPG monsters are pure nightmare fuel. Sure, there's a certain subset who are plain ol' cute, but for the most part they're a horrifying mash up of real world animals and mythical monsters, chimeric creatures amalgamating whatever bits and pieces the artist decided to chuck in the…
body: Not that I'm complaining, mind you—it wouldn't be a JRPG for me without them. I took absolute delight in Metaphor: ReFantazio's "humans" when I finally got around to playing it last Christmas, a wonderful take on the idea of what a monster even is, channeling Hieronymus Bosch's 500 year old paintings into some extremely distressing bosses.

But I never thought I'd find a top tier creepy JRPG monster in a Trails game. The series does have its darker moments, but for the most part, it's pretty homely and rustic, following the lives of regular folk. Trails in the Sky in particular is very chill, as you wander around Liberl as Joshua and Estelle, completing requests and odd jobs to earn their Bracer stripes.

However, while playing the Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter Remake recently, I ran into a monster in Kaldia Tunnel in the game's Zeiss region who freaked me out. The Faerie Epitaph was in the original game and kind of resembles a melted angel statue, but with this full 3D remake, Falcom added a fun trick to this monster.

articles.title: Microsoft Reacts To Xbox Game Pass Rumor That Could Change The Service In A Big Way
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a statement in response to a new rumor that claims the company is considering a massive shakeup to Xbox Game Pass in 2027 that would include numerous significant changes.
body: ResetEra user Slayven, who has accurately reported on unannounced Xbox news before, said the changes could include the bifurcation of Game Pass into two tiers: one with ads and one without. The tier with ads would be $13/month, while Game Pass without ads would cost $20/month, according to the report.

That's $3/month less than Game Pass Ultimate currently, and the price cut is reportedly reflective of another big change: Microsoft is reportedly removing day-one new releases from Game Pass starting in the February-April window of 2027. The rumor also stated that cloud-streaming access is being taken out of Game Pass, but people can pay for a $6 add-on that gets you 25 hours. Additionally, the report said a Family Plan will be available for an extra $6/month.

Beyond all of this, the report claimed there will be a tier of Game Pass that costs $15/month, and for that, people will get access to select titles in the Game Pass library, along with online multiplayer. Finally, it was reported that Microsoft will also offer a $11/month membership that provides access to online multiplayer alone.
points: Microsoft has released a statement in response to a new rumor that claims the company is considering a massive shakeup to Xbox Game Pass in 2027 that would include numerous significant changes.

articles.title: Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember isn't just a sequel - it's a culmination of everything Team Ninja has learned from Nioh, Ninja Gaiden, and Dead or Alive
articles.summary: The original Wo Long is an overlooked gem. Fast-paced, brutal, and compelling, the game made a name for itself amongst hardcore action-RPG aficionados because of its key gimmick: that basically every single attack could be deflected.
body: And why is that? It's because of Ninja Gaiden. Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember was in development alongside Ninja Gaiden 4, and you can tell. There's a "three-dimensionality" in this title that was lacking in the first game. In Wo Long, I would jump into most encounters, mostly because the slightly dopey AI wouldn't see or hear me coming, and I could land a fatal strike. It was an instant win. In Wo Long 2, though, you need to use your aerial attacks; it's baked into the entire combat system.

Maybe Team Ninja has internalised the criticism of the first game a lot, because whilst you can still deflect most attacks, even trash enemies have special moves that need to be dodged or countered, not just deflected. As a result, you need to get pretty dexterous with your hands, hitting the right combination of shoulder buttons and face buttons in some kind of unholy medley of Guitar Hero and Simon Says in order to survive even the most bog-standard enemy. Hey, it keeps you concentrating. Predictably, then, the learning curve is much steeper than in either the first Wo Long or Nioh, but the payoff is also more sublime.
points: Fast-paced, brutal, and compelling, the game made a name for itself amongst hardcore action-RPG aficionados because of its key gimmick: that basically every single attack could be deflected.

articles.title: James Pond Legacy Situation Is More Than Meets The AI
articles.summary: Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2. But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover.
body: If you go back and watch that trailer, it's not difficult to see why viewers pointed out the AI-like quality of the 3D characters adorning the game's box art and other promotional material. When System 3 responded to the accusations with the assertion that "no generative AI was used in the creation of the artwork," referring specifically to the Bovine Bomber character, this was based on the information it was given at the time by Antstream, the studio that handled the collection's actual development.

"That was the statement that we were given at the time by Antstream," System 3 CEO Mark Cale told GameSpot during a call. "We weren't involved in the process. They supplied all of the artwork and they supplied, in the process, the [work-in-progress] illustration. All of that was given to us."
Cale later provided GameSpot with the statement it received back in December from Antstream, well before the trailer was made public.
points: Last month, System 3 Software released a trailer for James Pond Legacy, a four-game collection for Nintendo Switch 2.
But the gameplay footage was largely overshadowed by accusations its developer used generative AI to create the game's promotional artwork and cover.

articles.title: The Last Of Us Season 3 Is Probably The Final Season, HBO Says Yet Again
articles.summary: HBO boss Casey Bloys has once again said that the upcoming third season of The Last of Us is expected to be its last. He told Deadline that Season 3 is coming in 2027, though did not confirm when in the year.
body: In January this year, Bloys was asked if Season 3 is going to be the last, and he said, "It certainly seems that way." However, at the time, Bloys admitted that a decision like that would come down to Mazin.
Before this, Mazin said that Season 4 was essential to bring the show to a conclusion. However, Bloys has indicated that the show may wrap up its run with Season 3, which could be a longer season.
“Craig is still working it out whether it will be two more seasons or one more long season. It hasn’t been decided yet, and I’m following Craig’s lead on that,” Bloys said in 2025.

In a big shift for the series, franchise creator Naughty Dog is not involved creatively in Season 3, and Neil Druckmann dropped out as a writer/director. People have speculated about what this could mean, but Druckmann, for his part, said he left the show to focus on his work on Naughty Dog's games.

videos.summary: Watch the ‘Catching Just Feel Right’ Live-Action Trailer for Aniimo, a free-to-play creature-collecting open-world game developed by Pawprint Studio. Players will hear the call to thrill and adventure to catch Aniimo, explore a vibrant open world, and harness new abilities along the way.
points: Watch the ‘Catching Just Feel Right’ Live-Action Trailer for Aniimo, a free-to-play creature-collecting open-world game developed by Pawprint Studio.
Players will hear the call to thrill and adventure to catch Aniimo, explore a vibrant open world, and harness new abilities along the way.
Aniimo is launching on September 16 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam and Epic Games Store), with a release on iOS and Android on September 23.
